title: Wrath on the Spiritual Assyrian
english: “…you have destroyed My land and killed My people; you will not remain for ever, evil seed. Prepare your children to be slaughtered for the sins of your father, so that they may not rise up and inherit the land and fill the land with war. And I will rise up against them, says the Lord of hosts, and I will destroy their name and remnant and seed” (Isaiah 14:20-22).

So the name of the Lord, he says, will come after a long time (Isaiah 30:27). If someone chooses to understand this historically, God took pity on Israel after seventy years. But if he follows the inner and hidden path of the meanings, he will grasp that the inventor of sin went on for a very long time laying the yoke of his own perversity on all who are on the earth, so as to make them his own worshippers and to bind them fast in the snares of sin. But after a long time the only-begotten Word of God appeared to us, and then came “wrath burning with glory,” and “the oracle of His lips, an oracle full of wrath” (Isaiah 30:27).

For Cyrus son of Cambyses, with God urging him on and rousing him to battle, marched against the land of the Chaldeans and took the land of the Babylonians by force. He became to them like wrath and fire, for he all but devoured them all; and since his assault could not be withstood, he appeared to those there like water rushing in a ravine, and filled all the nations of the Chaldeans with uproar and confusion, for they were justly condemned for vain error. For they supposed, as I said, that they had overpowered Judea even against God's will. So vain error seized them. For the effects of unmixed wrath were brought upon them by God, and they perished through their own impieties.

One may see the dragon, the author of evil, suffering this very thing. For the oracle of the Lord became for him an oracle full of wrath. He and the wicked powers with him were commanded to depart into the abyss (Luke 8:31). They were consumed as by fire, and, as though swept away by much water, they were carried by the power of the Spirit into the lowest depths. For these too were thrown into confusion for vain error.

For he said: “I will seize the whole inhabited earth in my hand like a nest, and I will take it up like eggs that have been left, and there is no one who will escape me or speak against me” (Isaiah 10:14). He supposed that he was truly God; and transferring to himself the glory that befits the Creator of all alone, he thought he could rule for ever over those on the earth. So they were thrown into confusion, condemned for vain error, and they were seized by it. For judgment, wrath and punishment were brought upon them, and for this reason.
“Must you always rejoice, and always enter My holy places as though keeping festival…” (Isaiah 30:29).

title: Until the Spirit Comes from on High
english: …the flocks of shepherds, that is, of the unclean spirits. So too the blessed David, framing his words as about Israel as a vineyard, says to God the Savior of all: “You brought a vine out of Egypt; You drove out nations and planted it” (Psalm 80:8). Then he adds: “Why have You broken down its hedge, so that all who pass along the way pluck its fruit? The boar out of the forest has ravaged it, and the solitary wild beast has fed on it” (Psalm 80:12-13).

For just as owners neglect the parts of their lands that have gone barren, and take no thought for them even if every kind of damage comes upon them, so too our God, who loves virtue, lets a soul go and leaves it stripped of all His sparing care, if it becomes empty of the fruits that make for good works.

“Until a Spirit from on high comes upon you. And Chermel will be a wilderness, and Chermel will be counted as a forest. And judgment will rest in the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in Carmel. And the works of righteousness will be peace, and righteousness will hold rest, and they will be confident for ever. And His people will dwell in a city of peace, and will dwell there in confidence, and will rest with wealth” (Isaiah 32:15-18).

He makes clear also the time at which the disobedient race from Israel will be empty of spiritual fruitfulness. For he turns the discourse, I mean, toward those who have honored our Lord Jesus Christ by their ready obedience, who have been cleansed through faith in Him and have come to share in the Holy Spirit. For what was foretold will come to pass, he says, and Israel will be laid waste for its unruliness, until a Spirit from on high comes upon you.

For as we read in the Acts of the holy apostles: “They were all gathered together in one place about the days of holy Pentecost. And suddenly there came from heaven a sound as of a mighty wind rushing, and it filled the house where they were gathered; and there appeared to them tongues dividing, as of fire, and they sat on each one of them, and they began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance” (Acts 2:1-4).

So when, he says, the Spirit of God from above and from on high comes upon you who believe, then Chermel too will be a wilderness. Chermel, or Carmel, is a very large mountain in Judea, thickly covered with dense woodland. So he likens to Chermel both Jerusalem itself and all the country around it, since it too had a countless multitude of inhabitants.
But it will be, he says, a wilderness, and will be counted as a forest. By forest he means wild woodland, which is of use for burning. For the untamed trees are cut down, and flame…

title: Zion, the City of Our Salvation
english: …through the lyre of the psalmist, saying: “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world” (Psalm 78:2; Matthew 13:35). And He spoke to the Jews too in parables.

So they did not give counsel to the people, he says, nor did the people know Him whose speech is deep. Nor did they give the counsel that would have kept the people from being called a despised people. For if they had given counsel, the people would not have been called despised; they would rather have been called blessed, as those who had recognized the Redeemer. But there was, he says, no understanding in the one who heard (Isaiah 33:19). For the Jews, being without understanding, did not test the voices of their leaders, nor discern whether they were giving good counsel or doing the opposite.

“Behold Zion, the city, our salvation! Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a rich city, tents that will not be shaken; the pegs of its tent stand for ever, nor will its cords be broken, because the name of the Lord is great to you. You will have a place, rivers and canals, broad and spacious” (Isaiah 33:20-21).

Between these come the words which God addressed to the senseless scribes of the Jews and to those who gave unholy counsel. Now the voice of the lovers of truth is brought in again, of those who have recognized the appearing of Christ and who say “Behold Zion,” meaning either the Church on earth or the fair city above in the heavens, the nurse of the saints. So whether one names the Church on earth or has that other city in mind, the thing shown by both will be one. For those who have been in the Church below will in due time be also in that city above, in the heavens.

Since, then, they all but leap for great joy at having recognized Zion, in which is our salvation, that is, Christ, and point it out to one another, at once the divine word takes up their words and says: “Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a rich city.” He speaks as if by likeness to the ancient tent in the wilderness. He calls Zion rich and says that the tent will be unshaken; for he declares that it has cords that cannot be broken and pegs fixed for ever. For the Church has been firmly set, and its continuance in well-being cannot be moved: “for the gates of Hades,” he says, “will not prevail against it” (Matthew 16:18).

And He gives the reason why it will be such, saying to those who have believed in Christ: “because the name of the Lord is great to you.” For to those who have not accepted the faith the name of Christ is not great and glorified; but with us who have believed it is great and exalted. For we worship Him as God, as truly the Son of the Father, as the Word made man for the salvation of all. This then, he says, the tent that abides for ever, is a place…
